A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work, renamed CoReLIN in v2. All main-text and appendix material is readable and matchable, including equations, tables, figures, and image-based prompts.

before.justification: V1 reports original ProcTHOR experiments, ablations, density and horizon analyses, and qualitative Spot robot deployments in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original simulation and hardware results and adds baseline comparisons, clutter-generation experiments, and quantitative failure analyses.

M1.justification: The frozen LLM, scene graph, cost/centrality reasoning, exploration, and Dijkstra/pick-place execution remain. The system and developer prompts are identical. Added descriptions of feasibility filtering, replanning, and exploration do not establish a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: The ProcTHOR tasks, 1–10-room coverage, and Spot setting remain. V2 Appendix G adds clearance-, degree-centrality-, and load-centrality-based clutter distributions, expanding environmental conditions within the same domain. The 10/15/20-task horizons already appeared in v1 Appendix G.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated ADIN and FastDownward baselines in Table 1 and Figure 5. InterNav also joins the 10- and 15-task comparisons, where it was absent from v1 Table 8, and ADIN joins the density comparison in Table 7. This substantially broadens comparator membership.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix C replace ratio-based LES with global min–max utilities aggregated geometrically, weighted 0.5 for success and 0.25 each for time and clutter. Added experiments specify new protocols, including FastDownward's 1800-second timeout and fully observed, 20-task clutter-policy tests. Existing splits and horizon coverage remain.

E4.justification: V2 adds LES sensitivity curves, tests dependence on three alternative clutter-generation policies, quantifies formatting and target-discovery failures, and provides three episode-stage case studies in Appendices C, G, H, and I. These substantially extend v1's retained manipulation-cost, history, model, density, and horizon analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's new failure percentages and average overhead measurements are additional outcomes rather than new uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: LES values and some rankings change under the revised metric; for example, DeepSeek overtakes GPT-5 in 4–6 rooms in Table 4. These are not same-metric performance gains. New baseline, clutter-policy, and failure results are added. Some raw entries also change: Table 7's unknown-map SR at d=0.5 in 4–6 rooms changes from 80.91 to 79.50.

T1.justification: The LES mathematical definition changes fundamentally from a normalized ratio to a weighted geometric mean with bounded min–max utilities, explicit exponents, and a numerical-stability constant. V2 also explicitly normalizes across the full evaluation set, replacing v1 Appendix C's floorplan-group normalization description.

C1.justification: The lifelong task, zero-shot constraint reasoning, and hardware-transfer contributions persist. The introduction changes its headline advantage over the strongest non-learned baseline from 20–50% to 16%, while the abstract foregrounds LES and PoC. The central methodological contribution and conclusion remain.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning fixed manipulation effort, small pick-and-place objects, and extreme clutter, plus explanations of discovery, formatting, and real manipulation failures. It recharacterizes Equation 2 as an analytical abstraction that is not explicitly optimized and revises interpretations of model-choice and clutter results.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds detailed ADIN action/reward/training adaptations and FastDownward PDDL construction, search, execution, and timeout information. Appendix G documents the new clutter samplers, and Section 3 expands implementation disclosure. The access statement changes from a promised release upon acceptance to reported code/data availability through a project webpage.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including NAMO-LLM, FLAX, RoboEXP, CuriousBot, and LLM-based robotics work. Section 2 explicitly contrasts NAMO-LLM's context limits and FLAX's simpler environments with the proposed setting. This refines the retained positioning around persistent, long-horizon interactive navigation.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the method CoReLIN, v2 substantially rewrites the abstract, baseline/model discussions, and LES and density exposition. Existing horizon material is integrated into the main comparison, a standalone limitations section is introduced, and the appendices are reorganized. Much core method and hardware prose remains.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two columns to a single-column layout with extensively rescaled and relocated displays. V2 Table 1 combines existing baseline/horizon material with additional rows, Figure 5 redraws the LES plot, and Figures 4 and 6–8 add sensitivity and walkthrough visuals. Existing hardware, dataset, and prompt images are retained.

improvement.justification: V2 improves comparison coverage and transparency through additional baselines, clutter tests, and failure/limitation reporting. However, revised quantitative reporting introduces unresolved inconsistencies: Table 1 gives InterNav SR=1.64% and LES=37.30 for g=10 in 1–3 rooms, exceeding Equation 4's maximum of about 12.81 at that SR. Tables 5 and 7 also now disagree on sparse-clutter results that matched in v1. These problems affect the central evaluation, preventing a reliable net-quality judgment.
